newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares extend morning losses in caution.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares extend morning losses in caution.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended early losses as selling accelerated in the second session on Wednesday amid caution ahead of Thursday's cabinet meeting, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 34 points, or 2.31 percent lower at 1,437, following a 1.16 percent drop in the morning. It had gained 1.94 percent in the past two days after diving 10.5 percent last week amid political tension.
Trade volume shrank to 20.07 trillion lira from Tuesday's 33.27 trillion.
"The trend depends entirely on politics. Tomorrow's cabinet meeting is awaited," said Niso Adato from Prim securities.

"There has to be a very positive development, like coalition partners fully agreeing on every issue and reinstating trust in the markets that the government will continue. The market needs this kind of morale," he added.

Measures to combat rising Islamist activism are expected to be discussed at Thursday's meeting, following a National Security Council (MGK) statement on February 28 which urged action against what the army saw as rising Islamist zeal.

Tension which had mounted early last week due to a row between the coalition's Islamist wing and the secularist army eased considerably after Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan signed the MGK statement last Wednesday.

Of the 237 shares traded, falls outdid rises sharply by 164 to 29 and 44 finished steady. The IMKB Industrial lost 2.51 percent to 1,473, the IMKB Services dropped 1.13 percent to 1,315 and the IMKB Financial shed 1.88 percent to 1,511.

Actives were led by largely state owned firms -- flat steel giant Eregli, down 1,250 lira at 16,750, oil refiner Tupras, down 3,000 lira at 52,000 and leading car maker Tofas, up 300 lira at 7,900. They made up about 25 percent of the total turnover.
